CCing Laura and Grace to advise on accounting treatment and journal routing. Hope we can close this today so Brian can get AP what they need.

Jonas / Team —

Thanks for flagging. Finance guidance below (high level):

• If the top‑up is intended as a direct reduction against an outstanding customer invoice, the correct instrument is a credit memo referencing the original invoice number. That allows AR to net without impacting recognized revenue.
• If we are issuing a promotional allowance not tied to a specific invoice (e.g., for marketing reasons), we treat it as a contra‑revenue allowance and record an allowance reserve at the time of grant.
• For short pilots with an intention to convert to a paid contract, we prefer credit memos where possible — simpler for AP reconciliation.

For Velosys specifically, we need: 1) a signed customer confirmation (simple attestation that they accept a $15k credit against their upcoming invoice), 2) the original invoice number to reference, and 3) the HubSpot deal id (I see D-98123-VE referenced by Jonas). I’ve attached a sample credit memo template and a proposed attestation wording below.

Proposed attestation wording (one‑line):
"Velosys confirms acceptance of a $15,000 promotional credit applied against Invoice #INV-20270430 issued by Redwood Inference. This credit will be reflected via a credit memo and may be offset against payable balances between the parties."

If AP needs DocuSign we can send that; otherwise a signed PDF works. Grace — can you confirm ledger mapping (G/L accounts) and whether Revenue Ops wants this posted to Promo Allowance (4100‑PROMO) or as Credit Memo Clearance (4200‑CREDIT)?

Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Laura / team —

Recommend the following ledger routing to minimize revenue recognition churn:

• Post the credit memo to AR as a contra entry against Invoice #INV-20270430. Use GL 4200‑CREDIT for the posting so it clears AR without touching recognized revenue accounts.
• If the customer does not provide an invoice number in time, record a short‑term Promotional Liability (GL 2305‑PROMO) and move to 4200‑CREDIT once the invoice reference is available.

I’ll prepare the Journal Entry examples and upload them to the shared drive, but for immediate AP needs the attestation Laura drafted is good. Karthik — flagging for any ERP mapping concerns; we may need to set the clearing code on the credit memo so NetSuite maps correctly.
